evidence.claim: Flagged transaction 3660353 occurred in billing region 87, which accounts for only 0.7% (2 of 281 prior transactions) of historical transactions on card C07871-K1.

The flagged in-person purchase 3660353 ($165.65) is the third in a cluster of card-present purchases in region 87 across three consecutive days (txn 3660351 for $193.94 on 2017-01-19, txn 3660352 for $207.74 on 2017-01-20, and txn 3660353 on 2017-01-21), demonstrating sustained travel rather than an isolated clone.

Between 2017-01-19 and 2017-01-21, card C07871-K1 engaged in no conflicting in-person transactions in other billing regions while active in region 87, with all other activity during this window being online transactions.

Device D000324 associated with transaction 3660353 is a generic desktop browser profile (Trident/7.0, Windows 7, IE 11) shared by 165 cards before the alert, with zero fraud or hot transactions in the window (lift 0.0).
Card C07871-K1 has no fraud ring association (ring_id -1, ring size 1) and device D000324 is linked to zero fraud ring cards.
Closed case CC-0270 on card C07871-K1 was an automated model alert for an out-of-region purchase ($1,504.02) that was cleared as legitimate travel after cardholder confirmation.

The alert text also contained 1 segment(s) addressed to the system rather than an analyst (outcome_directive, override, role_marker). They were set aside and used neither as evidence nor as instruction; the decision rests on the evidence above.

holder_baseline.how_to_read: If the holder's own prior transactions are confirmed fraud, this holder identity is compromised: matching its baseline is evidence FOR fraud, not against it. A holder is defined by card, billing region and anchor day, so its history is always in its own region: whether the region is new can only be read at card level (alert_context.card_history.flagged_region_share_of_card).

shared_origin.how_to_read: lift = share of transactions on this element scoring >= 0.5, divided by the same share across all transactions. Large regions and common email domains carry many unrelated cards; a shared origin needs lift well above 1 and several distinct cards.

assessment.reasoning: The alert was triggered on card C07871-K1 by an automated real-time risk score for transaction 3660353 ($165.65, in-person, product W) in billing region 87. Investigation of the graph shows that while region 87 represents an unfamiliar billing region for the card (only 0.7% of historical transactions), transaction 3660353 is part of a consecutive three-day sequence of card-present purchases in region 87 (txn 3660351 for $193.94 on 2017-01-19, txn 3660352 for $207.74 on 2017-01-20, and txn 3660353 on 2017-01-21). Crucially, during this three-day period there were zero conflicting in-person transactions in any home or baseline regions; all other transactions were online. Bank policy explicitly notes that several days of purchases in one new region indicates travel rather than card cloning. Furthermore, card C07871-K1 has no ring membership (ring_id -1), device D000324 is a generic desktop browser profile with zero fraud lift, there are no card testing sequences, and prior closed case CC-0270 on this card established a precedent of cleared model alerts due to legitimate travel. The alert is a false alarm representing legitimate cardholder travel.
